assessment.summary: Your strongest fit with this role is hands-on building: you have shipped a Python integration that calls an LLM API, handles rate limits and enforces a JSON schema. Your biggest gap is turning that technical work into customer value, since your pilot plan for a voice AI customer names a metric but not how you would scope, measure and explain it to non-experts. Strengthening your prompting depth and your voice build experience would also help you deliver tailored solutions for strategic customers.

dimensions.evidence_quote: Mostly Claude for writing and coding, and ChatGPT for quick questions.
dimensions.rationale: You use several tools for distinct purposes and have tried local models, though you do not use them day to day, so your range is practical rather than deliberate.

dimensions.evidence_quote: gave it an example of the format I wanted
dimensions.rationale: You provided context, audience, an example and a word limit, and iterated, which are good habits, but you showed only one worked example.

dimensions.evidence_quote: If it's code I run it and write a quick test.
dimensions.rationale: You have concrete, routine checks for code and facts, and you changed your habit after a real hallucinated API parameter, which shows strong practice.

dimensions.evidence_quote: The hard part was handling rate limits and getting consistent output, so I added retries and a JSON schema.
dimensions.rationale: You shipped a working API integration and addressed reliability problems concretely, though you did not mention evals, latency or cost.

dimensions.evidence_quote: I've used speech-to-text to transcribe meetings.
dimensions.rationale: You have used STT in practice and identified accent, noise, latency and disclosure concerns, but you have not yet built with text-to-speech or a voice agent.

dimensions.evidence_quote: I remove names and anything personal first.
dimensions.rationale: You check policy and remove personal data before using AI and prefer no-training tools, showing regular care though not depth on consent or bias.

dimensions.evidence_quote: agree a success metric like call handling time so we know if it worked.
dimensions.rationale: Your plan includes discovery, a one-use-case pilot and a success metric, which is a sound start, but it lacks detail on scoping, impact measurement and explaining AI to non-experts.

strengths: You have shipped a working Python integration that calls an LLM API, posts to Slack and handles rate limits with retries and a JSON schema.
You verify outputs in concrete ways: you run code with a quick test and cross-check facts against the docs after an invented API parameter.
gaps: Your customer delivery plan is high level: you name discovery, a pilot and a success metric, but not how you would scope, deliver and report impact to a strategic customer's engineers and executives.
Your prompting habits rest on a single example, so you would benefit from more systematic context, constraints and iteration for complex customer solutions.
You have not yet built with text-to-speech or a voice agent, so your voice experience is limited to transcription despite your interest in voice agents.

recommendations.title: Plan a customer pilot end to end
recommendations.why: The role owns delivery for strategic customers, so you need to scope a pilot, set measurable outcomes and explain them clearly to non-experts.
recommendations.first_step: Write a one-page pilot brief for a voice booking use case, with a scope, a success metric, a baseline and a short summary a non-technical executive could follow.

recommendations.title: Build a reusable prompt pattern
recommendations.why: Tailored customer solutions depend on getting consistent, high-quality output, which needs structured context and systematic iteration rather than one good example.
recommendations.first_step: Take your ticket classifier prompt and test three variants against 20 real tickets, changing one element at a time, and record which context and constraints improve accuracy.

recommendations.title: Add evals and latency checks to your integration
recommendations.why: Strategic customers will expect measured reliability, response time and cost, which your current build does not yet show.
recommendations.first_step: Create a small labelled set of tickets, script an accuracy check, and log the latency and token cost of each API call for one week.
